identity.title: OpenHOI: Open-World Hand-Object Interaction Synthesis with Multimodal Large Language Model

problem.claim: The paper addresses realistic 3D hand-object interaction synthesis for novel objects and language-guided, long-horizon manipulation.

gap.claim: Existing methods reportedly generalize poorly beyond closed-set objects and predefined tasks, especially for unseen objects and open-vocabulary instructions.

contributions.claim: OpenHOI is introduced as a framework for open-world HOI synthesis guided by free-form language and capable of generating long-horizon sequences for novel objects.
The approach combines a 3D MLLM for affordance grounding and task decomposition with an affordance-driven diffusion model and training-free physics refinement.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe OpenHOI as the first framework for open-world HOI synthesis.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that evaluations across diverse scenarios show superiority over state-of-the-art methods for novel object categories, multi-stage tasks, and complex language instructions.

narrative_sequence.summary: Realistic 3D hand-object interaction synthesis is framed as important for AR/VR and dexterous robotics.
Existing approaches are described as effective mainly for closed-set objects and predefined tasks, with failures on unseen objects and open-vocabulary commands.
OpenHOI is presented for open-world, language-guided synthesis of long-horizon manipulation involving novel objects.
A 3D MLLM grounds affordances and decomposes instructions, while diffusion synthesis and physics refinement target plausible, affordance-aligned interactions.
The authors report superior generalization across novel categories, multi-stage tasks, and complex instructions.

source_observation.claim: The abstract aligns each stated limitation with a corresponding capability: unseen objects and open-vocabulary instructions motivate open-world synthesis, while complex commands motivate affordance grounding and task decomposition.

lessons.interpretation: This makes the method-to-gap relationship easy to audit at the abstract level.
lessons.application: When introducing a new system, map each central failure mode to an explicit capability and state that mapping before presenting implementation details.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the work targets a narrow task and does not claim to address multiple distinct limitations.

unknowns: No quantitative metrics, dataset details, scenario counts, baseline identities, or statistical results are provided.
The abstract does not specify the relative gains or conditions underlying the reported superiority.
The claimed first-of-kind distinction is author-stated and not independently verified.
